Highlight Clip: Adam Back: Institutional Allocation Will Drive Bitcoin’s Third Wave of Adoption Adam Back: Institutional Allocation Will Drive Bitcoin’s Third Wave of Adoption On November 1, 2026, Blockstream CEO Adam Back said in an interview with Bitcoin Magazine that Bitcoin's first two waves of adoption were driven by individuals mining and buying Bitcoin, followed by ETFs. The third wave will broaden adoption through professional asset management channels but has yet to fully materialize. Some major investment banks have recommended a 2% to 4% Bitcoin allocation in their model portfolios. More people will gain indirect exposure through mutual funds, pension funds and insurance products, with Bitcoin treasury companies also playing a role. — link

Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Has Remained Below Its ATH for 374 Consecutive Days, Setting an All-Time Record Bitcoin's mining difficulty has spent 374 consecutive days below its all-time high of 155.97 T (set on October 29, 2025), officially marking the longest such stretch in the network's history and surpassing the previous 364-day record from the 2011 crash as well as the 253-day gap following China's 2021 mining ban. The protracted plateau is driven by muted BTC price action (~$76,000) and escalating overhead, prompting publicly listed miners to liquidate Bitcoin reserves and pivot site power toward AI colocation. — link

Users Report Deposit Restrictions at OKX, Binance and Other Exchanges Following FinCEN Action Against MEXC Following the U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issuance of a special measure order targeting MEXC Global, some community users reported that funds withdrawn from MEXC to centralized exchanges, including OKX, Binance, and Gate, were subjected to compliance reviews, held pending deposit crediting, or placed under refund review by the receiving platforms. Separately, Bitget Wallet confirmed that its card top-up service currently does not accept funds identified as originating from MEXC. FinCEN’s order has not yet taken effect. The exchange-related reports are primarily based on individual user accounts rather than official platform-wide restriction announcements. The scope of any restrictions and the eventual disposition of affected funds remain unclear. — link

Binance Names Justin Yek New CFO as Kaiser Ng Plans to Leave According to Bloomberg, Binance has appointed Justin Yek as its new chief financial officer (CFO), replacing Kaiser Ng, who is leaving to pursue a new venture. Binance co-CEO Yi He said Ng had been with the company for more than five years and that a transition plan had been in place for the past six months. Yek previously served as vice president of finance at Airwallex and head of Southeast Asia technology investment banking at Morgan Stanley. Ng previously served as CFO of Kraken. — link
